tasks.short: Meet teachers and the care team to develop teaching strategies and programs, schedule the meetings, and write up the agreed strategies.

steps.what: School psychologist collaborates with educational professionals to develop teaching strategies
School psychologist schedules meetings with teachers by e-mail
School psychologist writes up the agreed strategies and school programs

tasks.design: Meetings are scheduled with a shared-calendar poll ({CALENDAR}) instead of e-mail rounds. Strategies are written in a shared plan template with the school's set sections ({DOCS}), opened during the meeting, so the team sees the plan as it is agreed and nothing is mailed around afterwards. Developing strategies with colleagues stays with the psychologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Meetings were planned by e-mail and plans written up afterwards and mailed.
tasks.enabler_now: Calendar polls and shared plan templates are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Teachers have little time to meet.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a tired team to try one more approach.

reach.learn: Whether plans are clear and current.

evidence.claim: Calendar polls and shared document templates are standard office tools.

assumptions: Boundary: from the school question to the plan written; carrying out the strategy is outside.
Input contract: shared folders for the care team; fallback is e-mail.
Meetings do not get shorter. s3 keeps 80: the strategies are still written by the psychologist; only mailing drafts around and merging comments goes.
research_questions: Are plans shared sooner after meetings?

incremental.description: School psychologist keeps the plan template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: care teams keep e-mail rounds for dates (s2 keeps 80) and the plan is still edited after the meeting (s3 keeps 95) (3.0); high: calendar poll and shared plan as designed (11.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select the tests for the question, administer them to the child, score them against norm tables, and enter the scores in the student file.

steps.what: School psychologist selects psychological tests for the question
School psychologist administers psychological tests to the child
School psychologist scores tests: counts raw scores and looks up norm tables by hand today; after the change counts raw scores and enters them in the scoring software
School psychologist enters scores into the student file

tasks.design: Raw scores are entered once in the publisher's scoring software ({OTHER}), which converts them against the norm tables by fixed rules, so the psychologist does not look up tables by hand. The score report is stored in the student file without retyping. Selecting and administering tests and interpreting scores stay with the psychologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scores were looked up in norm tables and typed into the file.
tasks.enabler_now: Test publishers' scoring software converts scores against norms.
tasks.still_hard: Some older tests have only paper norms.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a child's low score comes from anxiety, not ability.

evidence.claim: Test scoring against norm tables can run as plain code in scoring software.
The psychologist stays accountable for test reports, including any AI use.

assumptions: Boundary: from the referral question to scores recorded; interpretation is outside.
Input contract: scoring software licensed per test; fallback is norm tables.
Testing does not change. s3 keeps 50 because raw scores are still counted and entered; only looking up norm tables goes.

incremental.description: School psychologist checks unusual converted scores against the table.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half the tests have licensed scoring software, so the rest are converted and typed by hand (s3 keeps 75, s4 keeps 60) (10.5); high: scoring software for all tests used (21.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review school records, observe the child in class, consult parents and school staff, and write the assessment notes.

steps.what: School psychologist reviews school records across several systems
School psychologist observes the child in class
School psychologist asks parents and school staff for consent to record the consultation and notes the answer
School psychologist consults parents and school personnel to assess the child's needs
School psychologist writes the assessment notes

loop.input: The recorded consultation with parents and staff, when all consent.
loop.output: A draft note in the file's structure.
loop.check: A validator flags any diagnosis or risk statement not in the transcript; the psychologist reads every drafted note against what was said and their own observations, corrects it and approves it.
loop.stop: One draft per consultation; if anyone declines recording or the draft is rejected, the psychologist writes the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: Consultations are free conversations; a form does not capture them.

tasks.design: A student view ({OTHER}) brings together grades, attendance, earlier reports and support plans from the school systems, so the psychologist does not search several screens. With the consent of parents and staff, a speech-to-note tool drafts the consultation note; a validator flags diagnoses or risk statements not in the transcript, and the psychologist corrects and approves every note. Observing and consulting stay with the psychologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Records were spread over several systems and notes typed after consultations.
tasks.enabler_now: Speech-to-note tools draft notes that the clinician corrects.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can add statements no one made.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a child's strength that the records miss.
tasks.altitude: The psychologist corrects drafts instead of typing notes.

evidence.claim: Dutch mental health care: 24 of 25 large providers use speech-driven reporting.
In a London child mental health clinic, median admin time per encounter fell from 27 to 10 minutes with ambient voice notes across 10 clinicians.
The psychologist stays accountable for AI-drafted notes.
Session notes and test results are health data under GDPR article 9.

assumptions: Boundary: from the referral question to notes written; the support decision is outside.

Input contract: consent for recording, asked and noted before each consultation (s3a); without consent, notes are typed as today. s4 keeps 65 because the observation and assessment parts of the notes are still written by the psychologist; only the consultation part is drafted.
research_questions: How often does the validator flag a statement?

incremental.description: School psychologist sorts out drafted notes where the recording failed or was unclear.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few parents consent to recording, so notes are mostly typed (s4 keeps 90), and the student view lacks earlier reports (s1 keeps 70) (7.7); high: most consultations recorded (16.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect outcome data from the student system and teachers' spreadsheets, analyse the data, interpret the results, and write the evaluation summary.

steps.what: Teachers enter program participation and behaviour incidents in the shared forms instead of their own spreadsheets
School psychologist collects data from the student system and teachers' spreadsheets
School psychologist analyzes data to evaluate program effectiveness in spreadsheets
School psychologist writes the evaluation summary

tasks.design: A versioned analysis script reads attendance, grades, behaviour incidents and program participation from the student system ({OTHER}) and teachers' shared forms into one store, and computes the standard measures per program, so data are not collected and combined in spreadsheets each time. The summary template fills tables and charts from the script's output, and the psychologist writes the conclusions. Interpreting results stays with the psychologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were collected from several spreadsheets and analysed by hand each time.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned scripts can read school data and compute standard measures.
tasks.still_hard: Teachers record behaviour in different ways.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a program works for some children and not others.
tasks.altitude: The psychologist interprets instead of collecting data.

reach.learn: Whether evaluations arrive in time for decisions.

evidence.claim: Versioned R, Python or SPSS scripts can replace hand-built spreadsheets for standard analyses.
Research on special-category data needs safeguards such as pseudonymisation.

assumptions: Boundary: from the program to evaluate to the summary written; program decisions are outside.
Input contract: teachers use shared forms; fallback is spreadsheets.
Teachers enter data in shared forms (s0, share 1, other role) in about the time their spreadsheets took. s4 keeps 70 because the conclusions are still written by the psychologist.
research_questions: Are evaluations ready before program decisions?

incremental.description: School psychologist maintains the analysis script.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many teachers keep their own spreadsheets (s1 keeps 70) and one-off evaluations need new measures (s2 keeps 80) (18.8); high: yearly evaluations with set measures (35.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The school psychologist keeps assessing children, testing, consulting and interpreting results; e-mail scheduling, norm-table lookups, typed notes and spreadsheet work shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A psychologist with more time with children.
